notes: **Group 2:** Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba, Ra. Two valence electrons (ns$^2$). Less reactive than alkali metals but still quite reactive.

**Physical trends:** atomic radius increases down group; density increases down group (except Be and Mg); melting and boiling points higher than alkali metals because of stronger metallic bonding from two valence electrons.
**Diagonal relationship:** Be and Al show similar properties (amphoteric oxides/hydroxides, covalent chlorides, complex formation) due to similar charge density.
**Compounds:** oxides and hydroxides are basic, but $BeO$ and $Be(OH)_2$ are amphoteric. Carbonates decompose on heating: $MCO_3 \rightarrow MO + CO_2$.
**Flame colours:** Ca brick red, Sr crimson, Ba apple green. Be and Mg give no colour.
